import Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Kaehler
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Torsion.Free

/-!
# Regular differentials inside rational differentials

For a domain with torsion-free differentials, localization in its fraction
field embeds the differentials into the rational differential space. Its
image is the regular differential lattice, with no choice of a local frame.
This is the local algebra used to assign orders to rational differentials.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped nonZeroDivisors

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

variable (k R K : Type*) [CommRing k] [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
  [Field K] [Algebra k R] [Algebra k K] [Algebra R K]
  [IsScalarTower k R K] [IsFractionRing R K]

/-- Torsion-free differentials inject into the differentials of the fraction
field under the natural localization map. -/
theorem differentialMap_injective_of_isFractionRing
    [Module.IsTorsionFree R Ω[R⁄k]] :
    Function.Injective (KaehlerDifferential.map k k R K) := by
  apply (IsLocalizedModule.injective_iff_isRegular R⁰
    (KaehlerDifferential.map k k R K)).mpr
  intro c
  exact (IsRegular.of_ne_zero (nonZeroDivisors.coe_ne_zero c)).isSMulRegular

/-- The regular differential lattice in the fraction-field differential space.
The definition uses the natural map, so it is independent of a basis. -/
def regularDifferentialLattice : Submodule R Ω[K⁄k] :=
  LinearMap.range (KaehlerDifferential.map k k R K)

/-- Localization identifies torsion-free local differentials with their
regular lattice inside the rational differential space. -/
def regularDifferentialLatticeEquiv [Module.IsTorsionFree R Ω[R⁄k]] :
    Ω[R⁄k] ≃ₗ[R] regularDifferentialLattice k R K :=
  LinearEquiv.ofInjective (KaehlerDifferential.map k k R K)
    (differentialMap_injective_of_isFractionRing k R K)

@[simp]
theorem regularDifferentialLatticeEquiv_coe [Module.IsTorsionFree R Ω[R⁄k]]
    (ω : Ω[R⁄k]) :
    (regularDifferentialLatticeEquiv k R K ω : Ω[K⁄k]) =
      KaehlerDifferential.map k k R K ω := rfl

end

end Hartshorne
